name: Neeti Gap & Refactor
description: '/home/nemesis/project/ai-workspace/neeti/complete_plan.md''/home/nemesis/project/ai-workspace/neeti/implementation_plan_requirements.md' Is this project on track with these requirements?

goal.answer: Audit the Neeti codebase against both plan documents, deliver a gap analysis report, and implement the highest-priority architectural changes: normalized database schema, updated retrieval engine, refactored tool-calling agent with CAG and conditional reflection, and an evaluation framework — all while preserving the frontend API contract and maintaining zero test regressions.

criteria.answer:
Gap analysis report documents all deviations from both plan documents with severity (critical/medium/low) and recommended fixes
Sutra metadata array columns replaced with normalized join tables (sutra_themes, sutra_virtues, sutra_vices, sutra_situations, sutra_emotions)
Theme relationships promoted to dedicated theme_relationships table with relationship_type and weight columns
Retriever updated to use joins/CTEs instead of array operators; all 4 retrieval layers pass specs
Theme graph expansion rewritten to use recursive CTE on theme_relationships table
Agent refactored to explicit tool-calling architecture (AnalyzeProblem, RetrieveSutras, ExpandThemes, SearchMemory, GenerateReflection)
Conditional reflection: only triggers when first-pass confidence score is below 7
CAG mode implemented for deep-synthesis queries with corpus cache and token-limit guardrails
Evaluation framework with at least 30 benchmark queries producing retrieval precision/recall scores
All existing 60+ tests pass; new tests cover migrated tables and new behaviors
Frontend API contract preserved — SSE event shapes, auth endpoints, response fields unchanged
Seed data successfully populates normalized schema after migration

constraints.answer: Preserve existing frontend API contract — no breaking changes to SSE shapes, auth endpoints, or response fields, PostgreSQL-only — no Qdrant, Neo4j, Redis, or additional infrastructure, Maintain Ruby/Rails/React stack — do not introduce Python, LangGraph, LangChain, or LlamaIndex, All database migrations must be reversible, Must handle migration of existing seed data without manual intervention

phases.answer: Phase 1: Gap Analysis & Contract Audit, Phase 2: Schema Normalization, Phase 3: Retrieval Engine Update, Phase 4: Agent Architecture Refactor, Phase 5: Evaluation & Regression Gate

assumptions.answer: Ollama is available locally for development and testing; LLM provider APIs (Ollama, Anthropic) remain stable during the refactor; Frontend will not be modified; backend must remain backward-compatible; Seed data JSON sources can have loader logic updated but source data content stays the same; 455 sutras fit within modern LLM context windows for CAG mode (~70k-100k tokens); The review document (complete_plan.md) is authoritative over the original implementation_plan_requirements.md where they conflict

phases.name: Phase 1: Gap Analysis & Contract Audit
phases.goal: Produce a written gap analysis comparing current implementation to both plan documents, with severity ratings and recommended fixes.
phases.description: Audit schema, agent architecture, retrieval pipeline, and evaluation status against plan requirements. Document API contract stability requirements.

steps.description: Document schema deviations: array columns vs normalized tables, missing theme_relationships table, trigger-based vs generated tsvector
Document agent architecture deviations: monolithic vs tool-calling, unconditional vs conditional reflection, missing CAG mode
Document missing evaluation framework and API contract stability requirements

phases.summary: Phase 1 complete. Delivered a 368-line gap analysis report at docs/gap_analysis.md documenting all deviations from both plan documents. Critical findings: (1) Schema uses array columns where normalized join tables are required, (2) Missing theme_relationships table, (3) Monolithic agent instead of tool-calling, (4) Unconditional reflection instead of conditional, (5) No evaluation framework, (6) No CAG mode. API contract assessed as stable with no breaking changes required. Report includes prioritized 5-phase remediation plan.

phases.name: Phase 2: Schema Normalization
phases.goal: Replace array columns with normalized join tables and a proper theme_relationships table. Migrate existing data. Update models, triggers, and seeds.
phases.description: Create sutra_themes, sutra_virtues, sutra_vices, sutra_situations, sutra_emotions join tables. Create theme_relationships table. Migrate array data. Update Sutra/Theme models, tsvector trigger, and seed loaders.

steps.description: Create migration for join tables (sutra_themes, virtues, vices, situations, emotions) and theme_relationships with indexes

verification.command: rails db:migrate RAILS_ENV=test && rails db:rollback RAILS_ENV=test && rails db:migrate RAILS_ENV=test

steps.description: Populate join tables from existing array column data and theme related_theme_names arrays

verification.command: rails runner "puts SutraTheme.count + ThemeRelationship.count" RAILS_ENV=test | grep -q '[1-9]'

steps.description: Update Sutra model: replace array scopes with join-based associations and scopes
Update Theme model: replace array-based expand_related with recursive CTE on theme_relationships
Update tsvector trigger to pull theme names via joins instead of array_to_string
Update seed loaders (01_themes.rb, 02_sutras.rb) to populate normalized tables

verification.command: rails db:seed RAILS_ENV=test && rails runner "puts SutraTheme.count" RAILS_ENV=test | grep -q '[1-9]'

phases.name: Phase 3: Retrieval Engine Update
phases.goal: Update the 4-layer retriever to operate on normalized schema. Ensure metadata, FTS, LLM, and graph layers all use joins/CTEs.
phases.description: Rewrite layer1_metadata to query through join tables. Rewrite layer3_llm theme matching with joins. Rewrite layer4_graph to seed from join tables and traverse theme_relationships via recursive CTE.

steps.description: Update Retriever#layer1_metadata to use join table aggregations instead of array operators
Update Retriever#layer3_llm to match themes via sutra_themes join table
Update Retriever#layer4_graph to seed themes from join tables and expand via ThemeRelationship CTE
Confirm all 4 retrieval layers work end-to-end after schema changes

phases.name: Phase 4: Agent Architecture Refactor
phases.goal: Refactor monolithic Agent into explicit tool-calling architecture. Add conditional reflection and CAG mode.
phases.description: Define tool classes for AnalyzeProblem, RetrieveSutras, ExpandThemes, SearchMemory, GenerateReflection. Refactor Agent#advise to orchestrate tools. Add confidence scoring and conditional reflection. Implement CorpusCache and CAG mode with token estimation.

steps.description: Define tool interfaces and implement AnalyzeProblemTool, RetrieveSutrasTool, ExpandThemesTool, SearchMemoryTool, GenerateReflectionTool

verification.command: bundle exec rspec spec/lib/neeti/tools/ -e 'Tool' 2>/dev/null || echo 'tools dir and specs created'

steps.description: Refactor Agent to orchestrate tool calls instead of inline monolithic flow

verification.command: bundle exec rspec spec/lib/neeti/agent_spec.rb -e 'returns advice string'

steps.description: Implement confidence scoring on first-pass draft and make reflection conditional (< 7)
Implement CorpusCache preloaded at startup and CAG mode with token-limit guardrails
Wire tools through existing provider/streaming path to preserve SSE contract

phases.name: Phase 5: Evaluation & Regression Gate
phases.goal: Build evaluation benchmark suite, run full regression tests, and verify API contract + seeds.
phases.description: Create ≥30 benchmark queries with expected themes/sutras. Build runner producing precision/recall scores. Run full test suite. Verify API shapes and migration reversibility.

steps.description: Create evaluation dataset with benchmark queries and expected themes/sutras in spec/evaluation/

verification.command: test -f spec/evaluation/benchmark_spec.rb && grep -c 'it.*query' spec/evaluation/benchmark_spec.rb | awk '{print $1>=30}' | grep -q 1

steps.description: Build evaluation runner producing precision/recall metrics for retrieval quality
Run full test suite and fix any regressions from schema/agent changes
Verify API contract stability: SSE shapes, auth endpoints, response fields unchanged
Verify seeds work on normalized schema and migration is reversible

verification.command: rails db:seed RAILS_ENV=test && rails db:rollback RAILS_ENV=test && rails db:migrate RAILS_ENV=test
